item.title: Woman Seriously Hurt in Rear-End Crash Near Molino
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 22-year-old woman was seriously injured Thursday morning after her vehicle struck a commercial truck stopped on Stout Road near Molino, according to North Escambia emergency responders. The crash happened around 7:45 a.m. when the passenger vehicle rear-ended the truck, which was positioned mostly in the roadway. Escambia County authorities…
item.content:encoded:
A 22-year-old woman was seriously injured Thursday morning after her vehicle struck a commercial truck stopped on Stout Road near Molino, according to North Escambia emergency responders.

The crash happened around 7:45 a.m. when the passenger vehicle rear-ended the truck, which was positioned mostly in the roadway. Escambia County authorities responded to the scene and treated the driver for serious injuries.

Details about the exact nature of the woman's injuries or whether the truck driver was hurt were not immediately available. The cause of the collision is under investigation.

item.content:encoded:
A 25-year-old Pensacola postal employee has entered a guilty plea to federal charges involving mail theft and drug possession, according to the Department of Justice.

Divincent Madison Jr. faces charges stemming from his work at a local postal facility. The case highlights ongoing concerns about package and mail security within the federal postal system.

Details about the specific amounts of mail allegedly stolen and the quantity of marijuana involved were not immediately disclosed in the initial announcement. Madison is scheduled for sentencing at a later date, where a federal judge will determine his punishment.

The U.S. Postal Service has emphasized its commitment to protecting the mail it handles and investigating misconduct by employees. Federal prosecutors have jurisdiction over crimes involving the mail system.

The University of Florida says the harmless flies typically swarm in April and May, then again in August and September. Numbers can vary widely from one part of the state to another. That…
item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Lovebug season is underway in Florida, and drivers across the state are getting reminders every time they hit the highway. The University of Florida says the harmless flies typically swarm in April and May, then again in August and September. Numbers can vary widely from one part of the state to another. That includes Northwest Florida. The university says lovebugs were first recorded in Florida in Escambia County in 1949. They don't bite or sting, but their remains can damage car paint if they're left on too long. The advice is simple: wash them off quickly. A damp cloth or dryer sheet can help remove the mess.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Whitney Lucas, chief of staff for the Escambia County Sheriff's Office, has been named one of the 2026 Top Women Chiefs of Staff by Women We Admire. Lucas reports directly to Sheriff Chip Simmons, helping shape the agency's strategic direction and policy work. She's also president of the Escambia County Sheriff Foundation, which she co-founded in 2021, and previously earned the Sheriff's Medal in 2023.

The road work is part of an $8 million project that also includes new classrooms to accommodate about 100 more students.

item.title: Study Links Birth Order to Disease Risk, but Experts Flag Data Gaps
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new study examining the connection between birth order and disease risk is raising questions about its completeness, as researchers acknowledge significant limitations in who was included in the data. The research found associations between birth order and certain health conditions, but excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid from the…
item.content:encoded:
A new study examining the connection between birth order and disease risk is raising questions about its completeness, as researchers acknowledge significant limitations in who was included in the data.

The research found associations between birth order and certain health conditions, but excluded uninsured families and those on Medicaid from the analysis. That means a substantial portion of the U.S. population—lower-income households that may face different health challenges and barriers to care—was left out entirely.

"The findings may not tell the whole story," experts caution. Researchers say a more accurate picture of how birth order affects disease risk would require future studies to include all income levels, not just insured populations. Without that broader data, scientists risk drawing conclusions that don't apply to everyone.

The limitation underscores a recurring challenge in medical research: studies based on incomplete or skewed populations can lead to incomplete or skewed results. Health experts emphasize that understanding disease risk across birth order requires looking at the full range of American families.

item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders have acquired wide receiver Stefon Diggs as they look to strengthen their offensive weapons heading into the upcoming season. The move addresses a priority for the team as they work to build a more competitive receiving group.

Diggs joins a Commanders offense looking to make strides after recent seasons. His addition comes as the team continues to evaluate its roster and make moves to improve performance on the field.

The move also reflects broader conversations around receiver evaluations across the NFL. Other players in the league, including some facing questions about their fit with new teams, have drawn scrutiny from multiple franchises regarding locker room dynamics and how they might integrate with existing rosters.

The Commanders will look to integrate Diggs into their system as they prepare for the season ahead.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

Schwartz will lead the CDC, the nation's premier public health agency tasked with disease prevention and coordinating outbreak response efforts. As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Senate has confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as the next director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention following a Wednesday vote by lawmakers. Schwartz will lead the CDC, the nation's premier public health agency tasked with disease prevention and coordinating outbreak response efforts.

As CDC director, Schwartz will oversee the federal government's primary institution for protecting public health and safety. The role involves managing disease surveillance, conducting epidemiological research, and coordinating with state and local health departments during health emergencies.

The confirmation of a new CDC director can have local implications for Escambia County and the broader Northwest Florida region, as the agency works closely with county health departments on vaccination campaigns, disease tracking, and emergency preparedness initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
Cesar Gastelum, a TikTok influencer with over 600,000 followers, has been killed in a shooting that occurred during a livestream outside a restaurant. Gastelum was broadcasting with two friends at the time of the incident.

Authorities are actively investigating the shooting. Details about the location, exact circumstances, and any suspects remain under investigation as officials work to piece together what happened during the livestream.

The incident marks a tragic loss in the social media community, where Gastelum had built a substantial following on the platform. As the investigation continues, authorities are expected to release additional details about the circumstances surrounding his death.

item.title: Sunny Skies, Lower Humidity Expected Through Friday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola area residents can expect pleasant weather conditions through the end of the week, with sunny skies and lower humidity levels making for comfortable outdoor conditions. Thursday will bring mostly sunny skies with highs near 89 degrees, according to the National Weather Service. Light east winds of 5 to 10 mph are expected, with gusts…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola area residents can expect pleasant weather conditions through the end of the week, with sunny skies and lower humidity levels making for comfortable outdoor conditions.

Thursday will bring mostly sunny skies with highs near 89 degrees, according to the National Weather Service. Light east winds of 5 to 10 mph are expected, with gusts reaching up to 20 mph. Overnight Thursday into Friday morning will remain clear with lows dropping to around 68 degrees and calm winds.

Friday looks even nicer, with sunny conditions continuing and highs climbing to near 91 degrees. East winds around 5 mph will become calm by afternoon, making for an ideal day for outdoor activities. The lower humidity levels accompanying this weather system should provide some relief from the typical summer mugginess.

Those planning outdoor plans through Friday should take advantage of the clear, stable weather pattern before conditions potentially shift over the weekend.

item.content:encoded: Firefighters quickly brought a vehicle fire under control Wednesday afternoon in front of the Davisville Community Center on Highway 97, according to reports from the scene. The blaze broke out while the vehicle was in motion on the highway before coming to rest near the community center. No injuries were reported as a result of the incident. Because the fire occurred while the vehicle was actively traveling on Highway 97, the Florida Highway Patrol has assumed the investigation into what caused the flames to ignite.

item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County man will spend the next 25 years in state prison following his conviction for a fatal shooting at a local gas station last year.

Arrington Marcellas Moultrie, 37, was found guilty of second-degree murder, shooting into a vehicle, and tampering with physical evidence related to the 2024 incident. According to court records, Moultrie was sentenced to the two-and-a-half-decade prison term as a result of the convictions.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about gun violence in Escambia County. Authorities did not immediately release additional details about the circumstances of the shooting or the victim's identity.

item.title: Escambia Animal Welfare Rescues Fox Tangled in Netting Near Molino
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A red fox is on the mend after getting trapped in netting on a property near Molino, thanks to quick work by Escambia County Animal Welfare officers. A resident on Stout Road spotted the distressed animal and called animal welfare dispatch for help. Sergeants Roberson and Agrecy responded to the scene and carefully freed the fox from the netting…
item.content:encoded:
A red fox is on the mend after getting trapped in netting on a property near Molino, thanks to quick work by Escambia County Animal Welfare officers.

A resident on Stout Road spotted the distressed animal and called animal welfare dispatch for help. Sergeants Roberson and Agrecy responded to the scene and carefully freed the fox from the netting that had become wrapped around it.

"Our officers were able to safely remove the netting and the fox is now recovering," according to the incident report from Escambia County Animal Welfare. The agency reminds property owners to secure netting and other materials that could trap wildlife, and to contact animal welfare immediately if they encounter an injured or entangled animal. Residents can reach Escambia County Animal Welfare dispatch for wildlife emergencies.

Thirteen of the 20 finalists will each receive grants of $101,000 during Impact 100's Annual Meeting scheduled for October 11. The grants…
item.content:encoded:
Impact 100 Pensacola Bay Area has selected 20 nonprofit organizations as finalists to compete for more than $1.3 million in grants, marking a milestone year for the women-led philanthropic organization.

Thirteen of the 20 finalists will each receive grants of $101,000 during Impact 100's Annual Meeting scheduled for October 11. The grants represent the organization's commitment to supporting community nonprofits across the Pensacola Bay Area.

The announcement comes as Impact 100 celebrates record membership. The organization now has 1,313 women members in 2026, an all-time high. Members pool their donations to support high-impact nonprofits through a competitive selection process, with each member having a vote in determining grant recipients.

item.title: Century Town Council Delays Decision on Street Department Employee Firing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Century Town Council has postponed action this week on a proposed termination of a street department employee facing allegations of gross negligence and causing financial hardship to residents, according to reporting from North Escambia. Under the town's charter, the mayor must obtain council approval before hiring or terminating municipal…
item.content:encoded:
The Century Town Council has postponed action this week on a proposed termination of a street department employee facing allegations of gross negligence and causing financial hardship to residents, according to reporting from North Escambia.

Under the town's charter, the mayor must obtain council approval before hiring or terminating municipal employees. The delayed vote suggests the council wanted additional time to review the case against the worker before moving forward with dismissal proceedings.

Details on the specific incidents cited in the negligence allegations were not immediately disclosed. The tabling of the motion means the matter will likely return to council at a future meeting for further deliberation and a final vote.

Lauralee Best received the gift from representatives of the Sun Belt Conference during a "Big Day for Teachers" event sponsored by the College Football Foundation. The Extra Yard for…
item.content:encoded:
A Tate High School educator was surprised with national recognition and a $1,000 award Wednesday as part of an annual initiative to honor outstanding teachers. Lauralee Best received the gift from representatives of the Sun Belt Conference during a "Big Day for Teachers" event sponsored by the College Football Foundation.

The Extra Yard for Teachers program celebrates educators across the country who make significant contributions to their students and communities. The award provides funds teachers can direct toward classroom needs or professional development.

Best's recognition reflects the Sun Belt's broader commitment to supporting education in communities across its member institutions' footprint. The conference has recognized teachers through this initiative for several years, highlighting the intersection between college athletics and K-12 education.

item.title: Alzheimer's Walk Coming to Foley in November
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Mobile Bay Walk to End Alzheimer's will take place November 14 at OWA Parks and Recreation in Foley, according to event organizers. The annual walk raises awareness and funds for Alzheimer's research and support services across the Mobile Bay region, which includes nearby communities in Northwest Florida. The event brings together families,…
item.content:encoded:
The Mobile Bay Walk to End Alzheimer's will take place November 14 at OWA Parks and Recreation in Foley, according to event organizers. The annual walk raises awareness and funds for Alzheimer's research and support services across the Mobile Bay region, which includes nearby communities in Northwest Florida.

The event brings together families, caregivers, and community members affected by Alzheimer's disease. Participants typically walk to honor those living with the disease and remember those lost to it.

For more information about registration, sponsorship opportunities, or to learn how to participate, organizers encourage interested residents to contact the event coordinators directly.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Semmes is bringing back its annual fall festival next month with a full slate of entertainment, food, and shopping. The free community event runs October 18 from 12:15 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. at Mary G. park, according to a city announcement.

Festival-goers can expect rides, vendor booths, and other attractions throughout the afternoon. The event draws families from across the area looking for a low-cost way to enjoy fall activities and local merchants.

Semmes, located north of Mobile, hosts the festival as an annual tradition to bring the community together. More details about specific vendors and activities are expected to be announced as the event date approaches.
